audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagree with their own why-text and with the packet chart: Level 1 reads Sylas at 7/10 while whys[0] says neither kit has a level-1 threat; Level 2 reads Skill while whys[1] says short exchanges go her way; Levels 4-5 reads Camille while whys[3] says neither side has a dominant window.
audit.why: A 42.66% win rate over 286 games is a losing lane, and a 7/10 Level 1 in a losing lane invites the exact early aggression that loses it.
audit.corrected: Level 1 reads Skill at 5/10, Level 2 reads Camille, Levels 4-5 reads Skill at 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere; the spikes and do's say only 'on Hookshot's cooldown'.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5s, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11s and The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90s against your Hijack at 80/55/30s. The R gap is the whole reason level 6 is yours.
audit.corrected: Hookshot's 12-16s and the 140s-vs-80s ultimate comparison written into the cooldown breakdown, spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Hookshot is called a stun in seven places — Riot's text says it knocks up. (b) Sylas's E is repeatedly called a stun ('before you have the stun to pin her', 'without your own stun landing first', 'no stun means she can kite') — Abscond/Abduct has no CC, the recast pulls him to the target. (c) True damage is attributed to her W cone; the trueDamage flag is on Precision Protocol (Q), while Tactical Sweep (W) is the slow-and-heal cone.
audit.why: Knockup versus stun changes what tenacity does for you. A stun Sylas does not have changes how he commits. And building against true damage on the wrong ability means itemising against the wrong half of her kit — armour does nothing about her Q either way, but Grievous Wounds is the answer to the W.
audit.corrected: Hookshot restated as a knockup; every phantom Sylas stun replaced with the chain pull; true damage moved onto Precision Protocol and the W named as the heal that Grievous Wounds answers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never mentioned even though Tactical Sweep heals her on the outer half of the cone and the entry's own plan is extended trades.
audit.why: Her sustain is the reason the mid-lane stretch is hers; anti-heal timing decides those exchanges.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in whys[3] and in the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Precision Protocol's auto-attack reset is never given as the burst tell.
audit.why: Her combo opens with the empowered attack, and the second cast hits far harder if she delays it — the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Named in whys[1] as the tell and the reason to step back between her two Q hits.

edits.before: - Camille Hookshot: matchup-defining — Her wall-dash stun — fight away from terrain while it is up. It governs your forward steps. - E1 shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Camille Hookshot: matchup-defining — her wall-dash knockup, 12-16s; fight away from terrain while it is up. - Her R is 140s at rank 1, yours is 80s — steal it and you own the rematch. - Hold the R for what decides something.

edits.before: Her wall-dash stun — fight away from terrain while it is up. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Her wall-dash knockup — stand off terrain while it is up. It is 12-16s; count it, then go.

edits.before: Track Camille’s Hookshot: Her wall-dash stun — fight away from terrain while it is up. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Camille’s Hookshot: a 12-16s wall-dash knockup — fight away from terrain while it is up. Down, or you don’t go.

edits.after: Precision Protocol's true damage comes online and Tactical Sweep heals through your return trade — the empowered-attack wind-up is your cue to step out, not the cast.

edits.before: Hookshot into a wall cancels your E2 approach angle and stuns you into a true-damage extended trade you are not built to win without your own stun landing first.
edits.after: Hookshot into a wall cancels your E2 approach angle and knocks you up into the extended trade her Q true damage wins — your chain pulls, it does not lock her down.

edits.before: Both kits are in play but neither has a dominant window — trade only around Hookshot's cooldown timer and respect her passive shield-break on the first Q hit.
edits.after: Neither side has a dominant window — trade inside Hookshot's 12-16s gap, buy Grievous Wounds so Tactical Sweep stops refunding her, and respect her passive shield.

edits.before: Camille's Q true-damage proc and W cone come fully online — she can force a favourable extended trade before your W heal and E stun can answer cleanly.
edits.after: Precision Protocol's true damage and the Tactical Sweep heal come online — she forces the extended trade before your W heal and chain pull can answer cleanly.

edits.before: Hijack steals The Hextech Ultimatum: you can cage Camille inside her own R, stripping her 1v1 isolation tool and swinging the all-in math.
edits.after: Hijack steals The Hextech Ultimatum on an 80s clock against her 140s: cage her inside her own R and she has no isolation tool left.

edits.before: Use E1 dash to absorb her W true-damage cone with the shield, then counter-trade with Q-W
edits.after: Dash E1 through the outer half of Tactical Sweep so she gets no heal, then counter with Q-W

edits.before: Land Hookshot into a wall to stun you and lock in the extended trade she wins with true damage
edits.after: Hookshot off a wall to knock you up and lock in the extended trade her Q true damage wins

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you have Q to poke CS steps but she matches it and your kit has no real threat yet; farm quietly and do not burn E chasing. At level 2 things get genuinely difficult: Camille's Q true-damage proc and W healing cone mean short trades consistently favour her, and without your full E stun you cannot punish her dive or create distance safely. By level 3 you have the full hook, but she can Hookshot into a wall to cancel your approach angle before E2 ever lands — respect terrain entirely and only take trades when her Hookshot is visibly on cooldown. Your Q slow and passive chain-autos deal real damage in extended exchanges, but her W true damage cuts through the W heal you're counting on.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have Q to poke CS steps but she matches it and your kit has no real threat yet; farm quietly and do not burn E chasing. At level 2 things get genuinely difficult: Precision Protocol's true damage and the Tactical Sweep heal mean short trades consistently favour her, and her second Q hits hardest when she delays it, so step out on the wind-up. By level 3 you have the full hook, but she can Hookshot off a wall to cancel your approach before E2 lands — respect terrain and trade only inside its 12-16s gap. Your Q slow and Petricite autos do real damage in extended exchanges, but buy Grievous Wounds or her W cone simply refunds them.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a genuine skill contest: you can short-trade with E1 shield into Q-W and walk out, but she can Hookshot-stun you and turn it into the extended fight she wins with true damage and her own healing W. Do not take a trade with both E charges spent — no shield means her W cone hits full, and no stun means she can freely auto-reset and kite. Level 6 is your real window: steal The Hextech Ultimatum and immediately look to cage HER — she loses her isolation tool and you can chain Q slow, passive autos, and W burst before she can disengage. Do not R a Camille who is under her own tower or already at full HP; the cage needs to be your offensive prison, not a free gift.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a genuine skill contest: you can short-trade E1 into Q-W and walk out, but a Hookshot knockup turns it into the extended fight her Q true damage and W heal win. Do not trade with both E charges spent — no dash means the outer cone lands and heals her, and you have no lockdown to answer the auto-reset. Level 6 is your real window: her R is 140s and yours is 80s, so steal The Hextech Ultimatum and cage HER — she loses her isolation tool while you chain Q slow, Petricite autos and W burst before she can disengage. Do not R a Camille under her own tower or at full HP; the cage is your prison, not a gift.

edits.before: Two items in, you are a genuine teamfight threat — stolen R from the most dangerous enemy, Riftmaker sustain, and E2 engage on an out-of-position carry are how you win games from this position. But do not 1v1 a Trinity Force Camille late: her Q true damage, W cone, and passive shield-breaker mean she consistently wins the extended duel your healing is supposed to win. Convert the Hijack advantage into objective control and kill pressure on her team, not a rematch top lane she will be favoured to win again.
edits.after: Two items in, you are a genuine teamfight threat — stolen R from the most dangerous enemy, Riftmaker sustain, and E2 engage on an out-of-position carry are how you win games from this position. But do not 1v1 a Trinity Force Camille late: Precision Protocol's true damage ignores every resistance you bought, and her passive shields against whichever type you deal. Convert the Hijack advantage into objectives and pressure on her team, not a top-lane rematch she is favoured to win again.

notes: Hookshot was called a stun in seven places and Sylas's own E in four more; neither is CC of that kind — hers knocks up, his only pulls. True damage was attributed to her W in three places when the flag and the tooltip put it on Precision Protocol. UNVERIFIED: every matchup in this champion's data says 'E1 shield', but Riot's Data Dragon text for Abscond/Abduct mentions no shield and the kit file carries no shield flag. I did not assert or remove it — if Abscond does not shield, the phrase 'E1 shield' is wrong across the whole champion, not just this entry, and needs a champion-level fix.
